← Interactive Chapter 10

Capstone · complete paper route

180-minute standalone core; calculator and paper/local document. Keep all plans, calculations, every trial, a 600–800-word memo, self-review and revised memo. No JavaScript or Python required. Optional Python +35 minutes is outside the core. Timing, rubric reliability and educational effectiveness await human validation.

Choose your evidence route · 20 minutes

CHAPTER 10 · LEARNING PROTOTYPE

Make the case.

Produce a 600–800-word research memo and an exportable evidence record. Answer: does the predefined rule improve the risk/return trade-off against its same-period benchmark after costs, and what remains uncertain?

Your 180-minute route

Orientation 20 · plan 20 · calculations 35 · memo 50 · self-review 25 · revision/export 30 minutes. Optional Python adds 35 minutes. Pacing and assessment effectiveness await human pilot validation.

OBJ-M10 / CLO-06: assemble reproducible evidence; distinguish observation from a forecast; meet every critical integrity item; self-assess against the analytic rubric and revise the memo. Profit is not a marking criterion.

Standalone path: the prepared plan below supplies the rule, costs, benchmark and evaluation block. If you completed Chapter 9, open its exported record beside this page and copy your question/prediction, including prior-inspection disclosure. There is no silent cross-chapter import. If you already saw evaluation results, disclose that the exercise is retrospective/exploratory. A fresh local plan is not proof of statistical preregistration.

Freeze a bounded question · 20 minutes

A bounded plan you can reproduce.

Use the prepared plan or copy your Chapter 9 question and prediction. You must freeze it here before ordinary-UI reveal, even on the standalone path. Public source files can expose the data: this is a learning gate, not secure blindness.

Rule: compare current close with the mean of the last three closes; position is long when strictly above, otherwise cash. Execute next open, earn the following open-to-open return. Start £1,000; cash zero; no shorting/leverage. Base 10bps and predefined 30bps cost sensitivity per traded notional. Benchmark same eligible dates and capital, entry and final exit costs. No dividends, taxes, extra slippage or liquidity model.

Dataset qf-synthetic-evaluation-2026-v1 is an original deterministic synthetic sequence, Feb 1–16 2026; it is not historical market evidence. First three closes are warmup. Edits invalidate current evidence and require a new frozen version; inspected revised plans are exploratory and old attempts remain.

Copy the prepared question: “Does the fixed three-close rule improve the observed trade-off versus the same-period net benchmark?” Write your own prediction, prior exposure and all fixed conventions. Freeze version1 before reading results. If revising, preserve the original, record deviations and label later inspected work exploratory. The original plan cannot be replaced by a cleaned-up retrospective one.

Calculate and retain · 35 minutes

Keep the result traceable.

Reveal both cost cases. Hand-check the first eligible row before writing the memo: start × (1 − turnover × bps/10,000) × market factor. For a long position, market factor = next exit open / entry open; for cash it is 1. Terminal liquidation follows the last row. Export contains the full input data, plan versions, every trial and row-level results. Report total simple return = final wealth / initial − 1, with no annualisation.

For a discussion of risk, compare the displayed positive maximum-drawdown magnitudes for strategy and benchmark at both cost levels. Drawdown=100×(1−wealth/runningpeak); include initial£1,000, period-end wealth and final liquidation. A simple100→80→100path has20%maximum drawdown even though it ends unchanged. These are observed boundary losses, not intraperiod or future bounds. Do not imply that a higher final value proves a better risk-adjusted investment. This compact capstone assesses traceability, timing and judgment, not estimation of a stable Sharpe ratio from a tiny synthetic sample.

Write this ledger to your calculation attachment or use the input CSV with the Chapter8 paper formulas. No annualisation, no probability forecast. Record every recomputation and decision, including negative results.

Draft a research memo · 50 minutes

Draft 600–800 words.

Suggested scaffold: question and decision (80–100 words); source and chronology (100–130); method and matching benchmark/costs (130–160); calculation evidence and both cost cases (130–160); limitations and what would change the decision (100–150); conclusion and revision note (60–100). These are guides, not separate hard word quotas.

Include dataset/version, rule and timing, frozen-plan history and prior exposure; first-row hand calculation; base and sensitivity net wealth/returns with same-period benchmark; every trial, including negative results; at least three consequential limits; a conditional decision. Place full rows and trial log in the exported calculation attachment rather than pasting every row into prose.

Word count checks assignment length only. It cannot judge truthful sourcing, reasoning or writing quality. The criterion checklist and rubric below are learner self-assessment, not external marking.

Draft in a local document and count whitespace-separated words. Include provenance, timing, all trials, base/sensitivity and benchmark, reproducible hand calculation, three material limits and conditional decision. Attach ledger separately. Counting words does not assess quality.

Calibrate and self-review · 25 minutes

Calibrate the judgment.

Calibration A — rejection can earn full marks: a memo reports the versioned synthetic data and all trials, correctly hand-checks costs, uses next-open/matched dates, shows both net cases, and rejects deployment because one tiny synthetic period and simplified execution provide insufficient evidence. It explains three specific limits and revises a claim in response. If all details are traceable, the rubric permits 20+25+25+20+10=100; rejection earns no penalty.

Calibration B — profitable but unacceptable: “Our 18% proves it always wins” appears without a traceable calculation; the signal earns an earlier return, losers are omitted and the benchmark uses different dates. Illustrative scores: source 5/20, calculation 0/25, design 0/25, limits 0/20, clarity 2/10 = 7/100. Critical timing, traceability and selection defects block readiness regardless of prose polish.

These are illustrative anchored examples, not independent grader calibration. Compare your actual memo with each criterion. Self-score honestly; cite a passage or row supporting your judgment and identify a concrete revision. A 70-point self-score plus every critical item is a prototype readiness check, not a validated course grade or credential.

Critical integrity criteria (all required)

  • Synthetic provenance and dataset version identified; no claim of real-market profit.
  • Signal at close; first eligible next open; no future data in positions.
  • Strategy and buy-and-hold use the same eligible entry/exit dates and capital.
  • Per-traded-notional entry, switch and final-exit costs; benchmark entry/exit too; cash 0, taxes/slippage excluded.
  • Every run retained; base 10bps and sensitivity 30bps; no winning-case selection.
  • Headline values trace to exported rows and correct hand calculation; conventions stated.
  • At least three material limits; inspected evaluation labelled exploratory if plan changed.
  • Conclusion is conditional; no guaranteed future return, deployability or personal recommendation.

Analytic rubric

Data and reproducibility: 20 points

0: missing or false source. 10: synthetic source named but version or reproduction steps missing. 20: version, dates, inputs, row evidence and repeatable steps all traceable.

Calculations and conventions: 25 points

0: untraceable or materially wrong headline. 13: correct headline but missing hand check or units. 25: correct current run, full cost/return conventions and independently traceable hand check.

Timing, benchmark, costs and evaluation design: 25 points

0: future data or mismatched dates unresolved. 13: chronology/costs mostly right but trial/reveal history unclear. 25: next-open execution, same-date net benchmark, frozen bounded plan, every trial and inspection caveat explicit.

Interpretation and limitations: 20 points

0: guaranteed-profit or causal overclaim. 10: generic caveats with weak link to results. 20: evidence-based accept/reject/insufficient conclusion, both cost cases and at least three specific consequential limits.

Clarity and response to feedback: 10 points

0: no revision. 5: readable draft with superficial correction. 10: concise 600–800-word memo, clear claims and a specific revision linked to criterion evidence.

Self-score each criterion, total out of100. Below70 or any unresolved integrity item: revise and recheck. Record score, supporting passage/row and specific weakness. This is learner self-assessment, not externally graded competence.

Revise and export · 30 minutes

Revise the memo, then export.

After recording a self-review, return to the memo and change at least one claim or explanation. Here explain the change, its rubric criterion and supporting evidence. A revision note without a changed memo is insufficient.

The exported record contains all frozen plans, runs, self-reviews and revisions plus source data. Save a separate plain-text memo and the evidence JSON. Anyone reproducing it should use the named dataset, fixed rule and both costs; compare first-row arithmetic and final wealth. Exports do not import or synchronise progress.
